broadcasts.message: normalize.js final: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. Faithful processing. Non-string input returned as-is (spec only defines string). No shadowing. Ready for final integration.
Tokenizer final: correct regex, no shadowing, handles empty input. Ready for release.

Pipeline unchanged and correct. It relies on injected tokenize, builds first-seen unique array and null-prototype frequencies object. Handles empty token list (returns empty arrays and count 0). No prototype collisions. Ready for final integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 3: All three modules are stable and consistent. My normalize.js is correct per spec. Peers report no issues. Potential edge: non-string input returns as-is; spec only defines string behavior, so acceptable. NFKC may alter characters (e.g., ligatures) but required. No changes needed. Final round: keep same implementation, broadcast readiness.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 3: All modules stable. Tokenizer uses regex with global flag; reset per call. Handles empty, punctuation, apostrophes. No changes needed. Final round: confirm no shadowing and correct interface.
private_memories.integrator: Round 3: All files stable. Peers confirm no changes. Pipeline uses Object.create(null) for frequencies, safe for 'constructor' and other prototype keys. The 'in' operator on null-prototype object checks own properties only. No shadowing. Ready for final round.
